MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  MAY 17, 2023

1.  CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall
  Council Chamber.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Brown Schachter, Boothe, Combs, Martin,
  Munday, Persichina, Romanelli, Varner

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Nash

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Duran, LACSD

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, FEBRUARY
  21, 2023.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
COMBS to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 21, 2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A. REQUEST FOR GREEN-COLORED BIKE LANES

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. At the
last meeting, the committee requested information regarding the cost to install green-colored bike
lanes. The options were estimated and include: 1) full green bike lanes with extension through
signalized intersections; 2) full green bike lanes without extensions; and 3) green at the bicycle
symbol and arrow at the start and intermediate locations of the bike lane.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends the use of Option 3 – green at
bike lane symbol and arrow locations. It is recommended that the Traffic and Safety Committee
discuss the item, receive public testimony, and provide direction to staff regarding the use of
green-colored pavement bike lanes.

In response to a question by CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
stated there are approximately 50 locations for the proposed green at bike lane symbol and arrow
locations.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE, Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that the original requestor, Ms. Stapleton, made the request for full green bike lanes
due to safety concerns.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER inquired if there have been any accidents involving bikes and
asked about other bike lanes in the city. Director Wahba stated that there are other bike lanes in
the city, but they are not typically marked. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there are
not generally a lot of accidents in the city and bicycle accidents are infrequent.
COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE recommended option 3, but also would like to address bike
lanes on Highridge Road since kids are riding bikes to school.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, May 17, 2023
 COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that statistical information is necessary in order to
make this decision.

Director Wahba stated concerns with the aesthetic of installing green bike lanes.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that she has heard more concern from cyclists on Palos
Verdes Drive East and stated that Palos Verdes Drive North is perhaps a safer road on the hill.

Deputy Duran stated that he has taken reports on three accidents in the past year. In his
experience, the accidents are cyclists running into vehicles, and not vehicles running into cyclists.
In all instances, he does not believe green markings would have prevented these accidents.

A brief discussion ensued on the necessity for green bike lanes on Palos Verdes Drive North.

COMMISSIONER BOOTHE made a motion to recommend Option 3 and to look into bike lanes
on Highridge Road. The motion failed.

COMMISSIONER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI,
  DENY THIS REQUEST

AYES: Brown Schachter, Boothe, Combs, Martin, Munday, Persichina, Romanelli, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT: Nash
ABSTAIN:

B. PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH – PARKING IN MULTI-USE PATHWAY

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. There
have been vehicles parked in the multi-use pathway on Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN)
between Palos Verdes Drive East and London Lane (Dapplegray School). There are currently
only three existing signs along this area of PVDN. There are eleven additional “No Parking” signs
being proposed.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends the installation of “No Parking
Any Time” signs along the path. These signs would include the use of arrows for clear direction
to the motorists.
Director Wahba stated that enforcement is an issue, but additional signage is necessary.
A discussion ensued on additional signage and enforcement. There was also a suggestion to add
a red line along the roadway.
Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki suggested notification to residents via the city newsletter
reminding residents about “no parking” in the multi-use path.
COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS
to,
  RECOMMEND THE INSTALLATION OF FOUR NEW “NO PARKING” SIGNS ON PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE NORTH BETWEEN PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AND LONDON LANE
  (AT DAPPLEGRAY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL) AND REPLACE THREE EXISTING “NO
  PARKING SIGNS”.

AYES: Brown Schachter, Boothe, Combs, Martin, Munday, Persichina, Romanelli, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT: Nash
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that this recommendation will be presented to the City Council at its June
13 meeting. COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE reminded staff to also mention the notification to
residents.

C. POSTED SPEED LIMITS – INFORMATIONAL ITEM

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
explained the process of how speed limits are posted in the City. She stated that the number used
for majority of drivers is the 85th percentile speed, which is the speed at which 85% of drivers are
travelling. This is considered the reasonable speed of a roadway. The 85th percentile speed,

Minutes, May 17, 2023
 reported collision history, and roadway characteristics not readily apparent to motorists are the
primary factors considered when determining the posted speed limit of a roadway.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER expressed concerns with the speed at which vehicles are
travelling on PVDN.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked about a calculation which would round to 40 mph as
opposed to the existing 35 mph. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that in this instance, it
coincides with other segments.

In a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that
the 85th percentile has been an agreed upon threshold/standard and this captures how an
overwhelming number of drivers normally drive.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the speed limit is reviewed every seven years. The
last Engineering Traffic Survey was adopted by City Council in 2021.

D. PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST - PEDESTRIAN
  CROSSING CONCERNS.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. At the
last meeting this item was discussed, and the committee asked for additional data. This item was
presented to the City Council and their recommendation was to install “Turning Vehicles Yield to
Pedestrians” signs with flags and they are in place now. In addition, the curb was painted red.

The data includes counts for vehicles, adult and school aged pedestrians, cyclists, skateboarders,
etc. Due to the delay in obtaining the data, this item will be presented at the next Traffic and Safety
Committee meeting to allow staff sufficient time to analyze the data.

Director Wahba stated that at the last meeting there was discussion on recommending the
installation of “No Right Turn on Red” signs; however, due to dealing with the island at Hitching
Post Drive and other reasons, staff recommended against the “No Right Turn on Red” signs.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that the intersection changed after the island at Hitching
Post Drive was installed.

John Owens, 19 Hitching Post Drive, stated that he does not believe that traffic would back up
anymore than it does now with the addition of a “No Right Turn on Red” sign since the intersection
clears quickly on green. Mr. Owens stated that there is also a decorative bus stop on that corner
which adds to the lack of visibility of pedestrians. He expressed his concern with drivers making
a right turn and are often only looking left for vehicles and not paying attention to pedestrians
crossing from their right.

Paul Moilanen, 31 Hitching Post Drive, expressed his concern with more children crossing the
intersection with the development of the new Nature Center and Founder’s Park.
He is particularly concerned with the southbound side; the other side is not as concerning since
there is a multi-use path.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI asked if a traffic study was done for the new Nature Center.
Director Wahba stated that this has been done.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE, Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that a model could be produced with the traffic counts that were taken showing how
traffic would be affected with the installation of “No Turn on Red” signs.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that “No Right Turn on Red” during certain hours may be
helpful as well.

Director Wahba expressed concern with pedestrians having a false sense of security when the
signs are installed, and this must be considered as well.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that this item should be considered for the next Traffic and
Safety Committee meeting where the results of the study will be presented. COMMITTEE
MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that the entire intersection should be considered for review at the
next meeting.

 6..  DIRECTOR ITEMS

A.  DEEP VALLEY DRIVE PEDESTRIAN IMPROVEMENT UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Director Wahba stated that there were residents from the mixed-use residential buildings present
at the last City Council meeting who are concerned with the safety of pedestrians crossing Deep
Valley Drive. This committee has discussed the Local Roadway Safety Plan that was adopted.
The city has applied for Highway Safety Improvement Plan grants; there is verbal approval to
spend $250,000 on Deep Valley Drive. Staff would like to move forward and have asked Willdan
to put together a proposal for the design work for the crosswalks. The proposal from Willdan will
be presented to the City Council. Within the next two years, Deep Valley Drive will be repaved,
and this project may coincide with this work.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI, Director Wahba stated that
once the design has been prepared for Deep Valley Drive, the proposed design will be brought
back to the Traffic and Safety Committee for review prior to being presented to the City Council.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked about the signage at Masongate Drive. Director Wahba
stated that the northbound/downhill “Trail Warning” signs were relocated but are now hidden by
a tree; staff will look into having the tree trimmed back.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that there was a recommendation to have “Horse Crossing”
painted at the crosswalk. She stated that a survey should be done prior to any decision to do this.

In response to a question by Deputy Duran, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that speeding
typically occurs in the neighborhood during the early morning hours.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked about conducting a survey. COMMITTEE MEMBER
BOOTHE stated that there are not too many equestrians in the neighborhood, and it may not be
helpful.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that the sign, when visible, plus the added enforcement
should help. This item can be revisited at a later date, if there is no improvement.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY inquired about the timing of the green traffic light at Palos
Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East. Traffic Deputy Itagaki stated that there is a
heavy demand and only one lane and it is difficult to get all the vehicles through in addition to the
other movements at Portuguese Bend Road and Rolling Hills Road.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that she has seen senior citizens come down from Silver
Spur Road to Palos Verdes Drive North and make a left onto the multi-use path and confuse it
with a street. She suggested installing a post (to work as a barrier) in the middle of the multi-use
path.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 7:43 p.m.
